facts.statement: The type species Protosqualus sigei was discovered in an Albian-aged rock deposit in France.
facts.quote: The type species is Protosqualus sigei, which was found around an Albian-aged deposit in France.

facts.statement: The name Protosqualus translates to "primitive Squalus" because it is an ancient relative of the modern genus Squalus.
facts.quote: The name Protosqualus means "primitive Squalus" in reference to how it is an ancient genus related to the modern genus, Squalus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Protosqualus teeth are frequently found in the Grey Chalk deposit in England.
facts.quote: Protosqualus teeth are quite common in the Grey Chalk deposit of England.

facts.statement: Protosqualus went extinct at the end of the Cretaceous period, with the last known species, P. argentinensis, found in southern Argentina and possibly earlier deposits in India.
facts.quote: The genus went extinct at the end of the Cretaceous during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, with the last species in the genus being Protosqualus argentinensis from southern Argentina as well as possibly being from earlier deposits in India.

facts.statement: Protosqualus teeth feature an undulated ventral margin on the dental crown located distal to the apron.
facts.quote: Protosqualus has an undulated ventral margin of the dental crown that was distal to the apron.

facts.statement: Unlike modern Squalus sharks, Protosqualus dental crowns did not exhibit a high degree of labiolingual compression.
facts.quote: Unlike modern members of the genus Squalus, Protosqualus has dental crowns that lacked a high degree of labiolingual compression.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. sigei possesses teeth with small gaps between them, each ending in a clearly defined slanted tip.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. sigei features a tooth with small gaps between them, each with a clearly defined slanted tip.

facts.statement: Protosqualus argentinensis is believed to have been the largest member of the genus, characterized by defined serrated cutting edges on its teeth.
facts.quote: Protosqualus argentinensis had defined serrated cutting edges and was probably the largest member of the genus.

facts.statement: While P. barringtonensis teeth may have exhibited sexual dimorphism, all teeth in this species display a short cusp.
facts.quote: Protosqualus barringtonensis may have shown some sexual dimorphism in the teeth, however all teeth show a short cusp.

facts.statement: Protosqualus is classified as a member of the family Squalidae within the order Squaliformes.
facts.quote: Protosqualus is a member of the Squalidae within the Squaliformes order.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Adnet and Cappetta identified Protosqualus as the sister taxon to the genus Squalus.
facts.quote: In 2001, Adnet & Cappetta found the following position for Protosqualus, recovered as the sister taxon to Squalus.

facts.statement: Protosqualus lived between the Barremian and Campanian stages, approximately 125.77 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Campanian (125.77 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Protosqualus shared Cretaceous oceans with other chondrichthyans, fish, and marine reptiles like mosasaurs and plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Protosqualus lived alongside other chondrichthyans as well as other types of fish. It also lived alongside marine reptiles such as mosasaurs and plesiosaurs in the Cretaceous oceans.

facts.statement: The Calafate Formation, where Protosqualus fossils have been found, likely consisted of estuaries and shallow seas.
facts.quote: The Calafate Formation likely had estuaries and shallow seas.

facts.statement: Some Protosqualus species, including P. barringtonensis, exhibit high levels of heterodonty, meaning their teeth vary significantly in shape.
facts.quote: Some species, such as P. barringtonensis, exhibit high levels of heterodonty.

rejected.statement: The genus Protosqualus was named in 1977 by the paleontologist and ichthyologist Henri Cappetta.
rejected.quote: The type specimen of Protosqualus was named in 1977 by paleontologist and ichthyologist, Henri Cappetta.
